# Balance & Quota · dsh-balance-meter
> A small plugin for DeepSeek Harness: **it tells you how much credit or quota is left for the model
you're actually using.**
No control panels to open, no mental arithmetic, and no being fooled by a stale number — if it genui
nely can't read your balance, it says why.
Click it to open the full panel:
## What problem it solves
Running an agent on API credit or a subscription, two things bite:

1. **You run out mid-task** and only find out when it breaks.
2. **You juggle several dashboards** —
DeepSeek, Kimi, Zhipu — and they don't even report the same thing: some give money, some give perce
ek, Kimi, Zhipu — and they don't even report the same thing: some give money, some give percentages.
This plugin gathers it into one place: **whichever provider your current session is using, it reads
that provider's balance** and shows it the same way every time.
## What it can read
Balances are **per provider**, not per model — every model under one provider shares the same pool.
### ✅ Supported: 9 built-in providers
| Provider | What it reads | Shown as |

| **DeepSeek** | account balance | money (`¥12.34`) |
| **OpenRouter** | key credit | money |
| **Mo

onshot / Kimi** | account balance | money |
| **SiliconFlow** | account balance | money |
| **智谱 GLM

/ Z.AI** | subscription quota | window percentages |
| **Kimi Coding** | subscription quota | windo

w percentages |
| **MiniMax** | plan quota | window percentages |
| **OpenCode Go** | subscription q

uota | window percentages |
| **OpenDesign (AMR)** | wallet + Design Plan windows | money + percenta

| window percentages |
| **OpenDesign (AMR)** | wallet + Design Plan windows | money + percentages |
"Window percentages" means the plugin lists each quota period separately — rolling / weekly / monthl
y — with its own bar and reset time. So you can tell whether the 5-hour window is nearly spent or th
e monthly total is running out.

If you use a **self-hosted relay** (New-API, Sub2API, CloseAI, claude-code-hub and similar), the plu
gin tries a set of conventional endpoints in order:

Whichever returns a readable figure first wins. **An endpoint you configure yourself is tried before
ns a readable figure first wins. **An endpoint you configure yourself is tried before all of them.**
> The mechanism (ordering, short-circuiting, unit calibration) is covered by tests, but **each prese
t's response shape was transcribed from public panel documentation and the author cannot verify them
all against live servers**. So an unrecognised shape is reported as "reachable but unparseable" wit
h the raw response attached — never guessed at.
### ❌ Not supported
| Situation | What happens |

| **The vendor has no public balance endpoint** | Says so plainly; invents nothing |
| **Route isn't

in the catalog and no preset matched** | Reports "not catalogued" plus the last raw response |
| **

No credential configured** | Names the variable you need to set |
| **Endpoint answered but the shap
e is unknown** | Reports "unparseable" with an excerpt (secrets masked) |
"Not catalogued" means **this plugin doesn't recognise that provider yet** — it does not mean the ve
ndor has no balance endpoint. Setting a custom endpoint via `balance_set_endpoint` usually fixes it.

## Using it
Mostly you don't do anything. Three ways in:
1. **Glance** — the readout is always on the stats row: money for API credit, a percentage for subsc

riptions.
2. **Click** — provider, billing mode, endpoint, last-read time, and every quota window wi

th its own bar.
3. **Ask** — say "how much quota is left" and the agent calls the `balance_check` to

its own bar.
3. **Ask** — say "how much quota is left" and the agent calls the `balance_check` tool.
## On getting the number right
This is what the plugin cares about most. Three rules:
**1. It never guesses.** If it can't read a figure it says so and explains why. "Unavailable" beats
a plausible-looking wrong number.
**2. Stale figures are labelled.** If a refresh fails after a previous success, the readout keeps sh
owing the last known value marked "possibly stale", with the failure reason in the details. An old n
umber is never passed off as current.
**3. The trend chart uses real readings only.** That curve comes from reads that actually happened,
not a hardcoded sample series. With fewer than two readings it says it's still collecting rather tha
n drawing a fake history.
### When it refreshes automatically

- **After each finished turn** — refreshed once
- **A background check every 15 seconds** — refreshe

s if policy allows
- **A reading older than 5 minutes** — forced refresh (configurable)
- **You clic
k "Refresh now"** — always
[该节后续省略]
## Privacy

- **No `exec` permission, no subprocesses** — no shell, no curl.
- **Requests go only to the gateway

you configured** — no third-party domains, no telemetry, no phone-home.
- **Keys are used for that
gateway only** — read from DSH's credential store, put in a request header, never written to disk, l
ogs, or the browser snapshot. The snapshot carries variable *names* only (there's a test asserting t

his).
- **Nothing else in DSH is modified** — only this plugin's own config row.
